- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 3–8% to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is bullish; cap early forecast values at 10% below true 30d mean.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model often underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for latent volatility.
